issues.description: Class Animal visibility mismatch: the problem statement (UML and explicit note) requires the name getter and setter to use protected visibility (UML shows protected members and the text at line 88 instructs to implement the name getter and setter with protected visibility). The reference solution (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) declares the constructor, getName(), and setName(...) as public. This contradiction between the specification and the reference implementation can confuse students about the intended access level for subclass inheritance and encapsulation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the artifacts consistent. Either (A) adjust the solution implementation to match the specification by declaring getName() and setName(...) as protected (and, if desired to match the UML precisely, change the Animal(String) constructor to protected), or (B) update the problem statement/UML to state that public visibility is acceptable for the constructor/getter/setter. Prefer (A) if the exercise intends to teach protected visibility; prefer (B) if tests or other provided code require public access.
